planting.note: Plant dormant canes in early spring as soon as ground can be worked; Anne is a fall-bearing (primocane) raspberry that fruits on the current season's canes, so it can be mowed to the ground each winter for a single heavy fall crop.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, slightly acidic, well-drained soil and irrigate consistently during fruit development. Anne is a large-fruited, primocane (fall-bearing) raspberry notable for its pale golden-yellow fruit, an unusual color among raspberries, with a rich, sweet flavor often described as more complex than standard red types. As a primocane variety it fruits on the current season's new canes, so the simplest pruning method is to cut all canes to the ground in late winter, sacrificing an early summer crop in exchange for one large, heavy fall harvest and eliminating the need to sort live from dead canes. It benefits from afternoon shade and consistent moisture in hot climates, since raspberries generally struggle with intense summer heat.
